rootCause: getTeamCalendar(@Query('month') monthStr: string) declares month as required in Swagger (@ApiQuery required:true) but performs NO runtime validation. When the request omits ?month=, monthStr arrives undefined and line 166 `const [yearStr, monthNumStr] = monthStr.split('-')` throws `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'split')`, which the StructuredExceptionFilter converts to a generic HTTP 500 instead of a 400. The real UI (TimeManagementPage.tsx) always derives month via monthStr(year, month) with year/month defaulting to the current UTC date, and fetchTeamCalendar(month: string) always appends `?month=${month}`, so the param is never empty in normal product flows. The 500 only manifests when a client (e.g. an adversarial probe) calls the endpoint with no query params. Same class of bug exists in sibling endpoints getCompliance (controller:209) and others (skill-match, my-time/month) per staging logs.

suggestedFix: Validate the month query param before use. Either (a) make a MonthQuery DTO with class-validator (@Matches(/^\d{4}-\d{2}$/)) bound via a ValidationPipe so a missing/malformed month yields HTTP 400, or (b) guard inline at the top of getTeamCalendar/getCompliance: `if (!monthStr || !/^\d{4}-\d{2}$/.test(monthStr)) throw new BadRequestException('month query param is required (YYYY-MM)');`. The codebase already has a parseMonthQuery contract (src/modules/timesheets/application/contracts/month.query.ts) used by MyTimeController — note it has the SAME undefined-input bug (reading 'match'), so the fix should harden the shared parser to reject undefined with a 400 and reuse it here.

The wire param is ALWAYS present and well-formed (e.g. 2026-06) in real usage — never omitted.
